subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman with a family history of breast cancer asks about her risk of developing epithelial ovarian cancer. Her 42-year-old friend has never been pregnant, began menstruating at age 11, and continues to have periods. Both women want to know which factors lower the risk of this disease.
question: Which of the following is associated with a DECREASED risk of epithelial ovarian cancer?

options.text: Previous pregnancy, breastfeeding, or tubal ligation

explanation_correct: Epithelial ovarian cancer risk is reduced by factors that lower the number of lifetime ovulations: previous pregnancy, breastfeeding, oral contraceptive use, and tubal ligation. In contrast, advanced age, early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, endometriosis, and BRCA1/BRCA2 or Lynch syndrome mutations increase risk. Ovarian tumors are the most common adnexal mass in females over 55 and may present with abdominal distention, bowel obstruction, or pleural effusion.

explanation_incorrect.A: Early menarche and late menopause increase the number of lifetime ovulations and therefore raise ovarian cancer risk.
explanation_incorrect.B: Nulliparity increases risk because it is associated with a greater number of lifetime ovulations.
explanation_incorrect.D: A BRCA1 mutation is a strong genetic risk factor for epithelial ovarian cancer.
explanation_incorrect.E: Endometriosis is associated with increased ovarian cancer risk, particularly endometrioid and clear cell tumors.

educationalObjective: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, OCPs, and tubal ligation reduce ovarian cancer risk by decreasing lifetime ovulations.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 45-year-old woman has a 7-cm unilateral ovarian cyst discovered on ultrasound. Histologic examination reveals a cyst lined by a single layer of columnar epithelium with ciliated cells that closely resemble the normal lining of the fallopian tube. The lesion is benign.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Serous cystadenoma is a benign epithelial ovarian neoplasm and the most common ovarian neoplasm overall. It is lined by fallopian tube–like (serous) epithelium and is often unilocular. The malignant counterpart, serous carcinoma, is the most common malignant ovarian tumor, and serous tumors can be bilateral, especially when malignant. The cervical-type mucinous epithelium instead characterizes mucinous tumors.

explanation_incorrect.B: Mucinous cystadenoma is lined by mucus-secreting, cervix-like epithelium and is typically multiloculated and large.
explanation_incorrect.C: Brenner tumor is characterized by nests of urothelial-like epithelium with coffee-bean nuclei.
explanation_incorrect.D: Yolk sac tumor is a malignant germ cell tumor of children and young adults with Schiller-Duval bodies and elevated AFP.
explanation_incorrect.E: Granulosa cell tumor is a malignant sex cord stromal tumor with Call-Exner bodies and elevated inhibin.

educationalObjective: Serous cystadenoma is the most common benign ovarian neoplasm and is lined by fallopian-tube-like epithelium.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 40-year-old woman undergoes removal of a large (20-cm) multiloculated ovarian mass. The cysts contain a viscous, gelatinous mucus material. Microscopy shows tall columnar mucus-secreting epithelium, and the lining resembles the normal cervical epithelium. The tumor is benign.
question: Which of the following best matches this description?
explanation_correct: Mucinous cystadenoma is a benign epithelial ovarian tumor that is typically large and multiloculated, lined by mucus-secreting epithelium resembling the cervix. It contrasts with serous tumors, which are lined by fallopian-tube-like epithelium and are more often unilocular. The malignant counterpart, mucinous carcinoma, is rare and may be metastatic from the appendix or other GI tract, potentially producing pseudomyxoma peritonei.

explanation_incorrect.A: Serous cystadenoma is lined by ciliated fallopian-tube-like epithelium and is usually unilocular, not mucus-filled and multiloculated.
explanation_incorrect.B: Brenner tumor consists of solid nests of urothelial-like cells with coffee-bean nuclei, not mucus-secreting locules.
explanation_incorrect.C: Fibroma is a benign sex cord stromal tumor of spindle-shaped fibroblasts, not a mucus-secreting epithelial cyst.
explanation_incorrect.E: Mature cystic teratoma contains elements from all three germ layers such as teeth, hair, and sebum, not pure mucinous epithelium.

educationalObjective: Mucinous cystadenoma is a large, multiloculated benign tumor lined by cervix-like mucus-secreting epithelium.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 55-year-old woman has a small, solid, gray-white ovarian nodule found incidentally at surgery. Histology shows nests of transitional (urothelial-like) epithelial cells embedded in a fibrous stroma. The tumor cells have nuclei with longitudinal grooves described as coffee-bean nuclei. There is no atypia or invasion.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Brenner tumor is usually a benign, solid ovarian neoplasm composed of nests of urothelial-like (bladderlike) epithelium with characteristic coffee-bean nuclei. It is an epithelial tumor but lacks the glandular and cystic architecture of serous and mucinous cystadenomas. It is typically an incidental finding and carries an excellent prognosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Mucinous cystadenoma is a large multiloculated mucus-filled cyst, not a solid nodule of urothelial-like nests.
explanation_incorrect.C: Serous carcinoma is malignant, with psammoma bodies and stromal invasion, not a benign coffee-bean-nucleus nodule.
explanation_incorrect.D: Dysgerminoma is a malignant germ cell tumor of adolescents with sheets of fried-egg cells and elevated LDH.
explanation_incorrect.E: Thecoma is a benign sex cord stromal tumor that produces estrogen and presents with postmenopausal bleeding, not urothelial nests.

educationalObjective: Brenner tumor is a usually benign ovarian epithelial tumor with urothelial-like nests and coffee-bean nuclei.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 63-year-old woman presents with abdominal distention and early satiety. CT shows a large bilateral ovarian mass with ascites and omental thickening. Biopsy reveals malignant epithelial cells forming papillary structures with concentric laminated calcifications. Serum CA 125 is markedly elevated.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis, and what is the appropriate use of the CA 125 level in this patient?

options.text: Mucinous carcinoma; CA 125 is used for routine population screening
Immature teratoma; CA 125 is used to assess placental function
Fibroma; CA 125 is used to confirm Meigs syndrome
Yolk sac tumor; CA 125 is used to monitor AFP production
Serous carcinoma; CA 125 is used to monitor treatment response and relapse, not screening

explanation_correct: Serous carcinoma is the most common malignant ovarian neoplasm and is characterized by psammoma bodies, the concentric laminated calcifications described here. It is frequently bilateral and may be associated with pleural effusion and ascites. CA 125 is a tumor marker used to monitor response to therapy and detect relapse, but it is not a good screening test because of poor specificity. Bilateral involvement is typical of serous tumors.

explanation_incorrect.A: Mucinous carcinoma is rare and may be metastatic from the GI tract; moreover, CA 125 is not recommended for screening.
explanation_incorrect.B: Immature teratoma is a malignant germ cell tumor of patients under 20 with immature neuroectoderm, not psammoma bodies.
explanation_incorrect.C: Fibroma is a benign spindle-cell stromal tumor; Meigs syndrome is a clinical triad, not a CA 125 diagnosis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Yolk sac tumor produces AFP rather than CA 125 and shows Schiller-Duval bodies, not psammoma bodies.

educationalObjective: Serous carcinoma is the most common malignant ovarian tumor with psammoma bodies; CA 125 monitors response/relapse, not screening.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 58-year-old woman undergoes laparotomy for a large multiloculated mucinous ovarian tumor. Frozen section suggests primary ovarian mucinous carcinoma, but the surgeon notes extensive gelatinous material coating the peritoneum and omentum, described as omental caking. Further investigation reveals an occult appendiceal adenocarcinoma.
question: Which of the following best explains the peritoneal findings in this patient?

options.text: Primary serous carcinoma seeding the peritoneum with psammoma bodies
A germ cell tumor with peritoneal implants of immature neuroectoderm
Metastatic appendiceal/GI mucinous carcinoma causing pseudomyxoma peritonei
A sex cord stromal tumor producing estrogen and ascites
Ruptured follicular cyst with hemorrhagic peritoneal irritation

explanation_correct: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma is rare, and many cases are actually metastatic from the appendix or other gastrointestinal sites. When mucinous tumor implants spread throughout the peritoneum, they can produce pseudomyxoma peritonei, an intraperitoneal accumulation of mucinous material also described as omental caking. This is why an apparent primary ovarian mucinous tumor should prompt evaluation of the GI tract, especially the appendix.

explanation_incorrect.A: Serous carcinoma can seed the peritoneum but produces psammoma bodies and serous, not mucinous, material.
explanation_incorrect.B: Immature teratoma is a germ cell tumor with neuroectodermal tissue, not gelatinous peritoneal mucin.
explanation_incorrect.D: Sex cord stromal tumors such as granulosa cell tumor produce hormones, not mucinous peritoneal implants.
explanation_incorrect.E: A ruptured follicular cyst causes acute pain and possibly hemorrhage, not chronic pseudomyxoma peritonei.

educationalObjective: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma is often metastatic from the appendix/GI and can cause pseudomyxoma peritonei with omental caking.
